documents.name: temporal-model-spec.md
documents.text:
# Temporal energy model

The temporal-energy/v1 model walks piecewise-constant power segments with exact integer arithmetic. Energy is stored in millijoules (mJ) and power in milliwatts (mW); durations are whole seconds.

## Reserve rule

A trajectory is feasible when the stored energy never drops below the reserve at any segment boundary. The reserve for the demonstration mission is 2000 mJ.

## Saturation

Stored energy saturates at the capacity; energy above capacity is counted as spill and reported separately.

documents.name: monte-carlo-notes.md
documents.text:
# Monte Carlo reliability notes

The reliability estimate uses a fixed, predeclared sample count and a Philox counter-based stream indexed by absolute sample position, so chunking never changes which logical samples are evaluated.

## Interval

The confidence interval is a Wilson score interval. The default confidence level is 95 percent. The interval is not a worst-case bound.

documents.name: heat-solver-notes.txt
documents.text:
Heat solver notes.

The two-dimensional heat solver uses the explicit FTCS scheme in float64 on a uniform grid. The stability condition is r_x + r_y <= 1/2, checked exactly with rational arithmetic on the declared decimal parameters. An unstable timestep is refused before any work starts, and the refusal reports the maximum admissible dt.

Boundaries are fixed Dirichlet values. Snapshots are stored as npy files. The default grid for the demonstration is 256 by 256 cells.

documents.name: mission-glossary.md
documents.text:
# Glossary

Spill: energy that could not be stored because the battery was at capacity.

Work unit: the deterministic unit a quote binds; for temporal batches it is one verified scenario evaluation, for heat runs one million cell updates.

Reviewer: the designated principal whose signed decision certifies scientific acceptance. A reviewer key is held by the service (server-managed custody).

documents.name: checkpoint-format.md
documents.text:
# Checkpoint container

Checkpoints are packed into the metacoin-compute-container/v1 format with a magic prefix MCCT, member names restricted to .npy and .json, and a sha256 per member. The worker encrypts the container with age before storing it as an artifact of kind compute_checkpoint. The two newest generations are retained by default.
